submittedPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: corrected source-local included contact luminance mask S2 v2 for Sakiko CHAT MIST.
Input 1 is the personally inspected healthy S1v2 markup rebuilt from the clean original mother; input 2 is that exact original mother for distinguishing naturally bright room pixels. No held S2 or screenshot is an input. Same 1536x1024 canvas and coordinates.

Convert only the intentional white original receiver/contact selections from image 1 to white/soft-gray on pure black: short cushion contact immediately under the skirt/hip (including any genuine small underhem island), and the complete local soft floor receiving patch under/next to both original loafers. Preserve the original soft receiver perimeter tightly, not a big blank-floor pool.

CRITICAL: the intended tiny physical boundary overlap at the actual LOWEST OUTSOLE AND HEEL CONTACT RIM must remain WHITE and CONNECTED TO THE ADJACENT FLOOR patch. Keep the existing narrow 2–4 source-pixel bottom contact band along each original toe-to-heel curved lower contour in the selection. Never subtract an enlarged black shoe silhouette that would leave a thin black moat between white receiver and the actual figure. Only the lowest original contact band is selected; the rest of both shoe bodies, socks, legs, skirt/hands/hair/face remain black. The original RGB is later drawn once under MAX(F,S), so this narrow actual outsole overlap is deliberate and safe, not double-drawn.

All other naturally bright linen/window/lamp/flowers/curtain and the distant room must become black; compare input 2 rather than automatically select original white objects. Do not select full shoe uppers or full pillow/long empty bench, invent new shadows, shift/resize contours, fill rectangles or preserve any body detail outside the intentional tiny bottom-rim/contact overlap.
Output one opaque 1536x1024 luminance PNG, white selected contact surface plus the narrow source-local support boundary, natural gray antialias only, pure black elsewhere. No crop/shift/scale, text/labels/outline or new figure.
